Pauline — thank you for the opportunity to put this together. Everything in it comes from the records and from one MLS® pull run this week: every semi-detached raised bungalow that has sold in the pocket this year, the one that is for sale now, and the district and city figures behind them. We have not been inside yet, so the number here is an estimate from the records and the photographs; the walkthrough turns it into a pricing strategy. One thing shapes the whole document: the plan is to sell vacant. The main floor is rented month-to-month, and how that tenancy ends decides when the house can be listed and who can buy it — so it gets its own section, with the routes set out side by side. Our reading of the evidence is stated once, at the end, and labelled as ours.

Section 01 · The property

A 1965 semi-detached raised bungalow on a 120-foot lot facing Roding Park, with a renovated legal apartment below.

579 Roding Street is a three-bedroom semi-detached raised bungalow in the Downsview-Roding-CFB community, north of Wilson Avenue and west of Keele, directly across from Roding Park. The main floor is original and will need work. The lower level is the opposite: a legal one-bedroom-plus-den apartment renovated in 2022, with its own entrance and mudroom, an egress window, ensuite laundry and a built-in garage below — leased in April 2025 at $1,950 a month all-inclusive within eight days, and now vacant. The main floor is rented month-to-month at $2,800.

Two things are true at once. Across the city, semi-detached homes are holding — 211 sales in September at an average up 2% on last year, 104% of list. In this district they are not: W05's semi-detached average is down 16% and its median 12% on a small sample, and the only October evidence in the pocket is a sale conditional at $799,900 after four months. Buyers for a raised bungalow at Keele and Wilson are still there — the form's median has sat at $845,000–$895,000 every month this year — but they are paying the pocket's number, not the city's.

Board statistics stop at the district line, so we pull our own MLS® data on the 1st of each month — every sale in the five regions — before the board publishes. During your listing that means we see a shift in this pocket and respond to it while other agents are waiting for the report.

Section 04 · What the pocket did

Five semi-detached bungalows sold in the community this year, all between $800,000 and $895,000. Nothing semi-detached cleared $900,000.

SYNERGY's own extract — every freehold sale in Downsview-Roding-CFB from January to September — puts the subject's form in a narrow band. The five semi-detached bungalow sales ran $800,000 to $895,000 with a $885,000 median, at 96% of list. The detached bungalows next door, the pocket's main stock, ran $770,000 to $1,285,000 with a $965,000 median — the detached premium over a semi here is roughly $80,000 to $100,000. No semi-detached home of any style sold above $956,000.

Section 05 · What each sale tells us

The same house three times, and the photographs rank them: remodelled, original-and-immaculate, original-and-empty.

110 Victory Dr · Keele & Wilson

$895,000

Sold August 29 · 93% of list · 44 days on the final listing, 123 in total

The ceiling, and the lesson. A fully remodelled main floor — open kitchen with island, pot lights, hardwood — over a self-contained lower apartment, on a 30 × 122 lot with an attached garage, vacant and staged. It is the one sale in the set finished to a higher standard than 579 Roding upstairs. It also opened at $969,000 in April, was relisted at $1,049,000 in May, relisted again at $998,000 in July, and sold four months after it first appeared. Three listings to find $895,000.

19 Gade Dr · Keele & Wilson

$885,000

Sold July 10 · 95% of list · 65 days

Original and immaculate. Hardwood, oak kitchens upstairs and down, California shutters and newer casement windows, a finished basement with a gas fireplace, sunroom and walk-up — kept by one family and shown that way. It is the proof that an original interior in this pocket does not have to be discounted to the floor if it presents well. Listed at $968,800, reduced to $935,000, sold at $885,000: 91% of the original ask.

21 Gade Dr · Keele & Wilson

$845,000

Sold August 1 · 96% of list · 67 days

The closest comparable. Next door to 19 Gade, the same plan, original throughout — 1960s kitchen and bath, hardwood, a finished basement with a second kitchen and a gas fireplace — well maintained but empty and unstaged, with the roof done in 2020 and the furnace in 2009. A buyer paid $845,000 for honest original condition with a garage and two entrances, which is the starting point for a house whose upstairs needs work.

The pattern

Ranked by the photographs, the three sales run 110 Victory (remodelled — $895,000), 19 Gade (original, immaculate — $885,000), 21 Gade (original, empty — $845,000). The whole spread from empty-original to fully remodelled is $50,000, and the market paid $40,000 of it for presentation alone. 579 Roding sits below 21 Gade on the main floor and above all three on the lower level — and the only October evidence, 37 Newlin in Section 07, says original condition is worth about $800,000 this month.

The two anchors bracket the house: 21 Gade at $845,000 for honest original condition in August, and 37 Newlin at $799,900 for the same in October, in a lesser pocket with a ravine lot. 579 Roding's main floor sits below Gade's; its lower level sits above every comparable's — and well above Newlin's, which is original on both floors. The market has moved between the two dates. The midpoint of $825,000 is the reconciliation — and at $675 per square foot it is the lowest rate in the set, which is where the one house with an original-and-tired upstairs should land. Newlin's $673 says the same thing.

This estimate is built from the records and the photographs on file. A walkthrough — the state of the main-floor kitchen and bath, the windows, the roof and mechanicals, and the lower suite as it stands today — is what turns it into a pricing strategy. Until then, treat it as a well-supported starting point rather than a number to list at.

Section 07 · Who you would be competing with

One semi-detached raised bungalow is for sale in the search area right now — and it went conditional this week at $799,900, after four months and three price cuts.

The actives pull returned a single home of this form: 37 Newlin Crescent in Glenfield-Jane Heights, 2.5 km west across the Humber. It is the most useful listing in the document because it is the only October transaction. An original-condition estate sale on a ravine lot with a detached garage opened at $999,000 in June, dropped to $879,900, then $795,000, was relisted at $799,900 on October 15, and had a conditional buyer eleven days later. The buyers for original raised bungalows are there this month; they are paying about $800,000, and they punish an opening price that asks for more.

Section 08 · Two ways to price it

Two ways to price it — and why the number is not final until we have walked through.

Both columns assume the house is listed vacant and launches within a week of the move-out, with photography, the lower-suite story and the ad campaign ready on day one. The range in Section 06 is an educated estimate from the records; the strategy is finalized once we have seen the house.

The pocket's own history decides the approach. Every sale in the set opened higher than it closed and gave back 4–9% from the original ask; the one that opened highest took three listings. Buyers here read the days on market as carefully as the price.

Two ways to price it

List at $849,000 — price to the evidenceList at $799,900 — invite competition, offers reviewed on day 7
List price$849,000, moving to $829,000 if there is no offer by day 21$799,900, offers reviewed on the seventh day
Price per sq ft$695 — between 21 Gade's $711 and Newlin's $673$654 — below every number in the set, by design
What the sales showedThe three pocket sales closed at 93–96% of their final list; at that ratio $849,000 lands $790,000–$815,000, with the step protecting the upper endNewlin found its buyer in 11 days at this number after 95 days above it; the pocket sold one in five over asking this year
Likely outcomeA sale at $810,000–$830,000 inside 30–45 daysTwo or more offers and a sale at $810,000–$835,000 inside two weeks — or one offer near $790,000 and a decision
What favours thisControl of the price; room to negotiate; no risk of a single low bid setting the market's view of the houseSpeed and certainty; the widest buyer pool on day one; the only strategy that has produced an October buyer in this pocket

Section 09 · Selling vacant

Selling vacant: three ways to get there, and why one of them is the plan.

The main floor is rented month-to-month at $2,800; the lower suite is vacant. The plan is to sell vacant, because the buyers who set the comparable prices — owner-occupiers who paid $845,000 to $895,000 for the three sales — need the main floor empty on closing day. Investors read the house differently ($4,750 a month across both units is a 6.9% gross yield on $825,000), and they stay in the campaign either way. The three ways to reach an empty main floor are set out side by side; the mechanics of each belong with our in-house legal review, not in a listing plan.

Nothing here assumes what the tenants will agree to. The conversation with them comes first; the listing date follows it.

A · Vacant before listing (N11, agreed)B · Sell with the tenant in placeC · Vacant on closing (N12 after a firm sale)
How it worksA mutual agreement to end the tenancy on a set date, usually with an incentive and flexibility on the move-out; the house is listed emptyThe listing is marketed as an income property with both units' rents stated; the tenancy transfers to the buyerSold to a buyer who will occupy the main floor; after the sale is firm, notice is served for the purchaser's own use with the compensation the Act requires
Who can buyEveryone — owner-occupiers and investorsInvestors, and owner-occupiers prepared to carry the notice process themselvesOwner-occupiers who will accept a closing that depends on the tenant leaving
What it does to the numberThe full range in Section 06, with the full buyer poolBelow the range — the owner-occupiers who set the comparable prices are excluded, and showings depend on the tenantThe range on paper, less whatever a buyer takes off for a closing that depends on someone else leaving
Cost to youThe incentive, and the rent forgone between move-out and closing — against the full buyer pool and the cleanest closingNone up front; the discount is taken at the saleOne month's rent as compensation, plus the risk
TimingListing follows the agreed move-out; photography afterListing can start now; showings on 24 hours' notice to the tenantListing now; 60 days' notice after firming, which sets a long closing
RiskThe tenants decline — then B or CA smaller pool and a lower number, with showings dependent on the tenant's cooperationA tenant who does not leave on the date; a closing that moves or fails; the buyer's recourse against you
What favours thisFull buyer pool, best presentation, the cleanest closingSpeed, no incentive paid, no vacancyNo incentive paid and the price of a vacant sale — if the closing holds

Our reading

Route A is the plan. The owner-occupier pool that set every comparable price needs an empty main floor, and the only route that delivers it without closing-day risk is an agreement reached before the sign goes up. What that agreement looks like — the notice form, the incentive, the dates — is a legal conversation we coordinate in-house before anything is signed. If the tenants will not agree, Routes B and C are the fallbacks, and we price and time the listing accordingly.

What we do for your property

The lower suite is the story — and it gets told to two buyer pools at once.

579 Roding has one thing none of the comparable sales had: a renovated, legal, proven-income apartment. The campaign leads with it — to the family that wants to live upstairs with $1,950 a month paying down the mortgage, and to the investor who reads $4,750 a month across two units. Two audiences, two sets of creative, one listing.

Production

  • Professional photography — the main floor staged and painted, the suite as it is — shot and edited for MLS®, print and social
  • Videography and aerial drone — the park frontage and the lot from above; a walkthrough that sells the two-unit layout
  • Floor plans — both levels measured and drafted, with the suite's entrance and egress marked
  • The income sheet — both rents, the all-inclusive structure and the carrying math on one page for the investor file

Exposure

  • MLS® and full syndication — REALTOR.ca and every major portal, day one
  • Paid digital advertising, 24/7 — across our six pages for the life of the listing, with one creative for families and one for investors
  • Collaborator posts — the tour reel on all six team pages at once, then to the large pages we work with
  • Agent network — a personal call to every agent who has sold a raised bungalow in W05 this year, and the investor agents who buy two-unit homes
  • Database — featured to 30,000 contacts, including our investor and landlord list

On the ground

  • Painting and touch-ups — the main floor, arranged and coordinated by us
  • Staging — the main floor furnished and styled so an original interior reads as a canvas, not a project
  • In-house legal review — the tenancy route, the offer conditions and the closing — checked before you sign
  • Showing protocol — agent-accompanied, lockbox only once vacant; feedback to you within a day of every visit

Questions sellers ask

The things most people want to ask, answered before you have to.

Why not list higher and come down if we have to?

Because this pocket reads the days. 110 Victory opened at $969,000 in April and sold in August at $895,000 across three listings; 37 Newlin opened at $999,000 and found its buyer at $799,900 four months later. Every sale in the set gave back 4–9% from its original ask, and the ones that opened highest took longest. A price the evidence supports on day one is the shortest route to the best number.

Do we have to deal with the tenants before we list?

That is the plan. The three comparable sales all went to buyers who could move in, so the house is listed vacant. Section 09 sets out the three routes to an empty main floor side by side; our recommendation is an agreed move-out before the sign goes up, and the mechanics of that are a legal conversation we coordinate in-house, not something to improvise.

Does the upstairs need to be renovated first?

No. 19 Gade sold at $885,000 with a 1960s kitchen and bath because it was clean, bright and furnished. The Signature package paints and stages the main floor so an original interior reads as a canvas rather than a project. A full renovation before selling rarely returns its cost in this bracket; presentation does.

Is the renovated basement worth anything to a buyer?

It is the reason this house is not priced at the floor. A legal, renovated suite with a proven $1,950 all-inclusive rent is $23,400 a year toward a buyer's mortgage — the comparable sales had second kitchens, not apartments. The campaign leads with it, to families and to investors.

What will the sale cost?

At the Signature package, 5% plus HST — about $46,600 at $825,000 — plus roughly $2,000 in legal fees and any incentive agreed with the tenants. Your mortgage payout comes off after that; once we have the balance, the full figure goes on one page.

Is there tax on the sale?

This needs a review before listing rather than a guess. The house has been rented, so the usual principal-residence treatment does not simply apply, and the November 2022 transfer sets the starting value the sale is measured from — not 1965. Depending on what the house was worth then, the result may be a gain, nothing, or a loss — and a capital loss, if that is where it lands, can be carried forward indefinitely against future gains. Terrence is a CPA and will make sure the right questions are asked of your accountant before the listing goes live.

How long will it take?

The three comparable sales took 65, 67 and 123 days; the listing under contract took 106. Priced to the evidence, with vacant possession and the suite marketed properly, 30 to 45 days to an offer is the reasonable expectation, with a 30–60 day close after that.

Who will I actually be dealing with?

Terrence, on every call, showing and offer. The team is behind the file — a Broker for the contract, a law-trained partner for the tenancy and the agreement, and licensed agents to cover showings — but one person is accountable to you, and it is the one whose name is on this document.
